newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to light up world's longest dragon at handover.
newsitem.headline: HK to light up world's longest dragon at handover.

text.p: Hong Kong will erect what it believes will be the world's longest string of decorative lights, depicting a dragon, to mark the handover to China later this year, organisers said on Tuesday.

The 10,000-foot (3.3 km) dragon will stretch from the waterfront near the Star Ferry pier on Kowloon peninsula, along the Golden Mile tourist district and northward to Boundary Street which officially divides Kowloon and the New Territories.

Britain's 99-year lease on the New Territories, which makes up more than 90 percent of the landmass of the colony of Hong Kong, expires at midnight on June 30, 1997. But London will hand back the entire territory of more than six million people.

A spokesman for the organisers, a group of 400 pro-China organisations, said they believe the HK$7 million (US$905,000) illumination will be the world's longest and are seeking an entry in the Guinness Book of Records.
Workers will start assembling the dragon in March and it will light up on the night of the handover on June 30.
